title: OCO index place code B1 / B2 / B3 (Laudes)
prompt: Lauds rows on dates with two or three saints use B1, B2 (once B3), sometimes with TP / TpA appended. 37 index row(s). Examples: #1891 'Istorum est enim' 12/5|L|B1TpA p1024; #1783 'In velamento' 12/5|L|B2TP p1043; #1782 'In velamento' 12/5|L|B1TP p1043; #716 'Beatus vir qui suffert' 12/5|L|B2TpA pNone; #1182 'Dum esset rex' 16/10|L|B2 p1137; #3000 'Tu es Domine' 16/10|L|B1 p1149. Legend OCO pp1210-1213 does not define this code. Rows with it are held: the mapper (oco/oco_sigla.py) gives no lit_part_sources target, so identity can load but the assignment waits. Answer = what the code means and where the chant goes (service.part, epoch, option_txt). Carry-out: add the rule to oco_sigla.py, re-run oco/load_oco_lps.py, record it in oco/specs/README.md 'User rulings'.

options.label: n-th saint of the date
options.detail: B1 = Benedictus antiphon of the first saint listed on that date, B2 of the second, B3 of the third; LPS → LAUDS.antB on that saint's epoch (agent picks the slug from the page heading).

options.label: alternative antiphons
options.detail: B1/B2 are two alternatives for the same office → LAUDS.antB option 1 / option 2.
